detail: Full summary: Empirical (git 2.50.1): `git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}` exits 128 for a missing object (the peel fails before existence is tested); bare `cat-file -e <sha>` exits 1; `rev-parse --quiet --verify <sha>^{commit}` exits 1 with empty stderr for missing full AND short hashes, 0 printing the canonical full SHA for existing ones, 128 outside a repo. Any exit-code-1 assumption on the peeled cat-file form is dead code.
